says: The till's own patterns: how it does a common thing, and where it departs from what most tills do, with the reason.

patterns.name: Ring first, tab after
patterns.reason: Most tills start an order from the first item and keep a separate counter mode. Here a counter sale is a short visit, so one screen does both, and no guest count is asked.

links.quote: A counter sale is a short visit, so one screen does both, and no guest count is asked.

patterns.name: Options open on the tap
patterns.reason: A drink with choices opens its options at once, out of the tile, with the usual choice already ticked.

patterns.name: Seats as seen from the bar
patterns.reason: The room map shows the seats as the barista sees them from behind the bar; a free seat opens a tab there.

links.quote: The room map is a pane from the left, opened by the map button beside +. The till recedes behind it.

patterns.name: Sends on leaving, button early
patterns.reason: Forgetting Send is the common failure of an explicit send. The round goes when the barista leaves the tab; the button stays for an early send, and each line shows Not sent, At the bar, Served.

links.quote: A round goes to the bar when the barista leaves the tab. The Send button stays for an early send.

patterns.name: One reason, two effects
patterns.reason: Tap-for-actions and void-with-reason are kept; the reason list also holds comp, waste and staff drink, so the reason decides whether stock was used.

links.quote: Moves that are not a sale are taps with a reason. A void after sending is a counter-entry, never a deletion.

patterns.name: Manager PIN in place
patterns.reason: A manager types their PIN in place, once, for the blocked action; the barista stays on the screen they were working on.

patterns.name: A decline has three ways on
patterns.reason: A declined card says nothing was charged, then offers Try again, Another card, or Leave on the tab.
steps: Retry, another card, or keep the tab

patterns.name: The guest tips on the terminal
patterns.reason: Some tills let staff key the tip in; here the guest picks it on the card terminal, so staff never type one.

links.quote: The guest picks a tip on the card terminal; it is never typed in at the till.

patterns.name: Tabs keep working offline
patterns.reason: With the wifi down the till says so, tabs keep working, and card payments wait for the connection.
